stories.title: Jackson, progressive Maine senator-elect, backs Van Hollen for leader
stories.summary: Troy Jackson, the progressive senator-elect from Maine who defeated Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), announced Wednesday that he will support Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) to become the next Senate majority leader.
stories.why: Nominations reveal bargaining among a party’s factions.
stories.watch: Collins’s margin against the Republican candidate for governor, town by town.

stories.title: Sullivan concedes to Peltola nearly a week after Alaska Senate race called
stories.summary: Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska) has conceded the Alaska Senate race to Sen.-elect Mary Peltola (D) days after the race was called by major networks, including Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), The Hill’s polling partner.
stories.why: States run elections; federal actors and courts contest the edges.
stories.watch: Daniel J. Sullivan’s first-choice share compared with his 2.5% in the primary.

stories.title: Trump claims "fake economic numbers" were released before election
stories.summary: President Trump demanded an investigation into the Commerce Department's recent revising of the GDP, which happens routinely.
stories.why: Voters reward or punish the party in power for conditions they experience.
stories.watch: Whether vote choice tracks evaluations of the economy and the Iran war in exit polls and AP VoteCast, and whether places more exposed to fuel prices move differently.

stories.title: Judge declines to issue a long-term ban on taxpayer-funded, pro-Trump ads critics called propaganda
stories.summary: A federal judge on Wednesday sided against Democrats on the federal government's taxpayer-funded ads that promoted partisan messages and President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections, declining to extend a temporary ban.
stories.why: States run elections; federal actors and courts contest the edges.
stories.watch: Litigation over ballots and certification (California, Alaska) and court rulings on maps.

stories.title: Rhode Island voters reject bond measures for the first time in 20 years
stories.summary: The Rhode Island Board of Elections certified the Nov. 3 election results on Nov. 24, confirming that voters defeated both Question 3 and Question 4. This marks the first time voters have defeated a bond measure since 2006.
